questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) The effectiveness of any data communication system is based on THREE major components. State and explain the use of each of these components. (3 marks)

(b) Differentiate between synchronous and asynchronous data transmission. (2 marks)

(c) Describe the concept multiplexing as used in data communication. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Three major components of a data communication system (3 marks).**

- **The sender (source):** the device (computer, phone, sensor) that **creates the message and sends it** into the system.
- **The transmission medium (channel):** the **path that carries the signal** from sender to receiver: a wired medium (twisted pair, coaxial or fibre-optic cable) or a wireless medium (radio waves, microwaves, satellite).
- **The receiver (destination):** the device that **receives the signal and converts it back into a form the user can understand** (for example a computer, a printer or a phone).

(The message itself and the protocol, that is the set of rules which the sender and the receiver follow, are also listed as components in some courses; the data communication system works correctly only if the data arrive accurately, on time and complete.)

**(b) Synchronous and asynchronous transmission (2 marks).**

| | Synchronous transmission | Asynchronous transmission |
|---|---|---|
| How data are sent | In **large blocks (frames) in a continuous stream**, without gaps between characters. | **One character (byte) at a time**, with gaps between the characters. |
| Timing | Sender and receiver are **synchronised by a common clock (timing) signal**. | **No common clock**; each character carries a **start bit and a stop bit** so the receiver knows where it begins and ends. |
| Speed and cost | Faster and more efficient for large amounts of data, but more complex and costly. | Slower (extra start and stop bits), but simple and cheap. Example: keyboard to computer, serial port. |

**(c) Multiplexing (1 mark).** Multiplexing is the technique of **combining the signals of several senders into one signal that is sent at the same time over a single shared channel (medium)**; at the receiving end a demultiplexer separates the signals again. It makes better use of the expensive link (for example by frequency-division or time-division multiplexing).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Define the term Internet protocol. (1 mark)

(b) State the importance of HTTP protocol. (2 marks)

(c) State the function of a router in a network. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Internet protocol (1 mark).** The Internet Protocol (IP) is the **set of rules that governs the addressing of devices and the routing of data packets across networks**: each device has a unique IP address, and the data are divided into packets that are sent to the destination address.

**(b) Importance of HTTP (2 marks).** HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol that **allows a web browser (client) to request web pages from a web server and the server to send them back**. Its importance:

- it is the **standard set of rules for transferring web pages (hypertext, images, video) between server and browser**, so that the World Wide Web works on any computer;
- it allows **links to be followed and forms to be sent** to servers (its secure version HTTPS adds encryption).

**(c) Function of a router (1 mark).** A router **connects two or more networks** (for example a local network to the Internet) and **forwards the data packets towards their destination along the best path**, by reading the destination IP address of each packet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is database normalization? (2 marks)

(b) State three advantages for normalizing a database. (3 marks)

(c) Give two properties of a table in second normal form. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Database normalisation (2 marks).** Normalisation is the **process of organising the data of a relational database into well-structured tables, following a series of rules called normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF...)**, in order to **remove redundancy (repeated data) and unwanted dependencies** between the data. Large tables are split into smaller related tables linked by keys.

**(b) Three advantages of normalising a database (3 marks)** (any three):

- It **reduces data redundancy**, so less storage space is used.
- It **avoids update, insertion and deletion anomalies**: a fact is stored in one place only, so it is changed once.
- It **improves data integrity and consistency**: the same data cannot have different values in different places.
- The database is **easier to maintain and to extend**, and the structure is clearer.

**(c) Two properties of a table in second normal form (2 marks).**

1. The table is **already in first normal form**: every field holds a single (atomic) value and there are no repeating groups.
2. It has **no partial dependency**: every non-key attribute depends on the **whole** primary key and not on only a part of a composite key.
